name: Jira
description: A tool for bug tracking, issue tracking, and agile project management.

tools.name: Add Attachment
tools.description: Uploads and attaches a file to a Jira issue.

inputs.name: issue_key
inputs.about: The ID or key of the Jira issue to which the attachment will be added.

inputs.name: file_to_upload
inputs.about: File to be attached to the Jira issue. Supports various formats including images, documents, and other file types.

tools.name: Add Comment
tools.description: Adds a comment using Atlassian Document Format (ADF) for rich text to an existing Jira issue.

inputs.name: comment
inputs.about: The comment text. Supports Markdown formatting including **bold**, *italic*, `code`, links [text](url), lists, and @mentions. To mention users, use @username for single-word names or @"Display Name" for names with spaces. Plain URLs are not hyperlinked; use `[text](url)` format for clickable links.

inputs.name: issue_id_or_key
inputs.about: The ID or key of the issue to add the comment to.

inputs.name: visibility_type
inputs.about: Specifies the type of visibility restriction for the comment. Valid values are 'group' or 'role'. If this field is used, `visibility_value` must also be provided. IMPORTANT: 'group' visibility requires group-level visibility to be enabled in the Jira instance settings by an administrator. For 'role'

inputs.name: visibility_value
inputs.about: Name of the group or role that can view the comment (required if visibility_type is set). IMPORTANT: These values are instance-specific and vary by Jira configuration. For role visibility: Use JIRA_GET_PROJECT_ROLES with your project key to discover valid role names (e.g., 'Administrator', 'Member',

inputs.name: additional_properties
inputs.about: Additional properties to include in the comment request body. This can be used to pass extra fields supported by the Jira API that are not explicitly defined, such as 'properties' for EntityProperty objects. Format: {'properties': [{'key': 'myKey', 'value': {'myValue': 123}}]}.

tools.name: Add Field to Screen Tab
tools.description: Adds a Jira field to a screen tab. By default, Jira also updates field associations for projects linked to the screen; set skip_field_association to true to avoid that side effect.

inputs.name: tab_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the screen tab to which the field is added.

inputs.name: field_id
inputs.about: ID of the Jira field to add, such as 'summary' or 'customfield_10000'.

inputs.name: screen_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the Jira screen containing the tab.

inputs.name: skip_field_association
inputs.about: Whether to add the field only to the screen tab without associating it with projects linked to the screen.

tools.name: Add Users to Project Role
tools.description: Adds users or groups to a Jira project role. Users can be identified by account ID and groups by name or ID; group names and group IDs cannot be combined in the same request.

inputs.name: role_id
inputs.about: The ID of the project role to add users to. Use get_project_roles action to find available role IDs.

inputs.name: group_ids
inputs.about: Optional list of group IDs to add to the project role. Mutually exclusive with group_names (Jira's ActorsMap rejects sending both).

inputs.name: group_names
inputs.about: Optional list of group names to add to the project role. Mutually exclusive with group_ids (Jira's ActorsMap rejects sending both).

inputs.name: user_account_ids
inputs.about: List of Atlassian account IDs of users to add to the project role. Must be Atlassian account IDs (alphanumeric strings), not email addresses or display names; use JIRA_FIND_USERS to resolve account IDs first. Optional, but at least one of user_account_ids, group_names, or group_ids must be provided.

inputs.name: project_id_or_key
inputs.about: The project ID (numeric) or project key (e.g., 'PROJ') of the project.

tools.name: Add User to Group
tools.description: Adds a user to a Jira group.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The ID of the group to add the user to. Either group_name or group_id must be provided.

inputs.name: account_id
inputs.about: The Atlassian account ID of the user to add to the group.

inputs.name: group_name
inputs.about: The name of the group to add the user to. Either group_name or group_id must be provided. Must be an exact match; prefer group_id for precision.

tools.name: Add Watcher to Issue
tools.description: Adds a user to an issue's watcher list by account ID. Requires the authenticated user to have permission to view the issue and manage watchers; insufficient permissions may result in silent failure or an error response.

inputs.name: account_id
inputs.about: The Atlassian Account ID (accountId) of the user to be added as a watcher. Important: Usernames cannot be used due to Jira API privacy changes; the accountId is required. Resolve the accountId first using JIRA_GET_CURRENT_USER (for the calling user) or JIRA_FIND_USERS (for other users) before callin

inputs.name: issue_id_or_key
inputs.about: The ID (a numerical identifier, e.g., '10000') or key (a project-prefixed string, e.g., 'PROJ-123') of the Jira issue to which the watcher will be added.

tools.name: Add Worklog
tools.description: Adds a worklog entry to a Jira issue to record time spent. By default, it requests automatic adjustment of the issue's remaining estimate; other estimate adjustment options are available.

inputs.name: expand
inputs.about: Use expand to include additional information about the worklog in the response. Accepts 'properties'.

inputs.name: comment
inputs.about: Atlassian Document Format comment structure.

inputs.name: started
inputs.about: The datetime when the work was started in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2024-01-15T09:00:00.000+0000'). If not provided, the current time is used.

inputs.name: reduce_by
inputs.about: Amount to reduce the remaining estimate if adjust_estimate is 'manual' (e.g., '1h 30m', '2d').

inputs.name: time_spent
inputs.about: The time spent as a Jira duration string (e.g., '2h 30m', '1d', '45m'). Either this or time_spent_seconds must be provided.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.about: Details about the visibility restriction of a worklog.

inputs.name: new_estimate
inputs.about: The new remaining estimate if adjust_estimate is 'new' (e.g., '2h', '3d 4h').

inputs.name: notify_users
inputs.about: Whether to notify users watching the issue about this worklog.

inputs.name: adjust_estimate
inputs.about: Options for adjusting the issue's remaining estimate when adding a worklog.

inputs.name: issue_id_or_key
inputs.about: The ID or key of the Jira issue to add the worklog to.

inputs.name: time_spent_seconds
inputs.about: The time in seconds spent working on the issue. Either this or time_spent must be provided.

inputs.name: override_editable_flag
inputs.about: Whether to add the worklog even if the issue is not editable (e.g., closed). Requires admin permissions.

tools.name: Analyse Jira Expression
tools.description: Analyses Jira expressions for syntax validation, type checking, and complexity analysis. Use when you need to validate Jira expression syntax before using it in automation rules, custom fields, or workflows.

inputs.name: check
inputs.about: Type of check to perform on the expression.

inputs.name: expressions
inputs.about: The list of Jira expressions to analyse. Each expression will be checked according to the specified check type.

inputs.name: context_variables
inputs.about: Context variables and their types. The type checker assumes that common context variables (such as 'issue' or 'project') are available in context and sets their type. Use this property to override the default types or provide details of new variables.

tools.name: Assign Issue
tools.description: Assigns a Jira issue to a user, default assignee, or unassigns; supports email/name lookup.

inputs.name: account_id
inputs.about: The Atlassian Account ID of the user to assign the issue to. Use `'-1'` (as a string) to assign to the project's default assignee. Provide `None` (Python null, which translates to JSON null) or omit this field to unassign the issue. Takes precedence over assignee_name if provided. JIRA_FIND_USERS ma

inputs.name: assignee_name
inputs.about: Name of the user to assign the issue to. Can be either an email address (e.g., 'john@company.com') or display name (e.g., 'John Doe'). The system will auto-detect the type and search accordingly. Ignored if account_id is also provided. On Jira Cloud, privacy settings may cause lookup failures; prefe

inputs.name: issue_id_or_key
inputs.about: The ID or key of the issue to be assigned.

tools.name: Bulk Create Issues
tools.description: Creates multiple Jira issues (up to 50 per call) with full feature support including markdown, assignee resolution, and priority handling.

inputs.name: issues
inputs.about: List of issues to be created (1 to 50 per request). Each issue definition follows the same structure as the single create issue action. For subtasks, include parent_key to specify the parent issue. IMPORTANT: Priority names are instance-specific - use JIRA_GET_ISSUE_EDIT_META or try submitting to di

tools.name: Bulk Move Issues
tools.description: Submits an asynchronous bulk move of Jira issues using destination project, issue type, and optional parent mappings. Returns a task ID for tracking progress.

inputs.name: sendBulkNotification
inputs.about: Whether Jira should notify users about the moved issues.

inputs.name: targetToSourcesMapping
inputs.about: Destination-to-source mappings. Each key has the format '<destination project ID or key>,<destination issue type ID>' or adds ',<destination parent ID or key>' when moving to a subtask type.

tools.name: Check User Permissions
tools.description: Check user permissions for global and project-level operations in Jira. Use this action to verify whether a user has specific permissions at the system level or within projects. Useful for authorization checks before performing operations, or for auditing user access rights.

inputs.name: account_id
inputs.about: The account ID of the user to check permissions for. If not provided, checks permissions for the currently authenticated user. Account ID format: '712020:xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx' or '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g'.

inputs.name: global_permissions
inputs.about: List of global (system-level) permission keys to check (e.g., 'ADMINISTER', 'SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'CREATE_SHARED_OBJECTS', 'MANAGE_GROUP_FILTER_SUBSCRIPTIONS'). These permissions apply to the entire Jira instance.

inputs.name: project_permissions
inputs.about: List of project-level permission checks. Each item specifies permissions to validate along with optional project and issue IDs for context.

tools.name: Create Board
tools.description: Creates a new Jira board (kanban, scrum, or agility) with optional filter and location configuration. Use this action when you need to set up a new board for a project or create a personal board for tracking work. The board will organize and visualize issues based on the specified filter or project context.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name for the new board. Choose a clear, descriptive name that helps users identify the board's purpose.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: Type of board to create. 'kanban' for continuous flow boards, 'scrum' for sprint-based boards, 'agility' for basic agile boards.

inputs.name: filterId
inputs.about: ID of an existing Jira filter to use as the board's issue source. The filter defines which issues appear on the board. Use JIRA_LIST_FILTERS or JIRA_GET_FILTER_FAVOURITE to find filter IDs.

inputs.name: location
inputs.about: Location configuration for the board.

tools.name: Create Component
tools.description: Create a component in a Jira project.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Unique name for the component within the project.

inputs.name: project
inputs.about: Key of the project in which to create the component.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Description of the component.

inputs.name: assigneeType
inputs.about: Nominal assignee type for issues created with this component. Jira uses PROJECT_DEFAULT when this field is omitted.

inputs.name: leadAccountId
inputs.about: Atlassian account ID of the component lead.

tools.name: Create Custom Field Context
tools.description: Create a project and issue-type context for a Jira custom field.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name of the custom field context.

inputs.name: field_id
inputs.about: ID of the custom field for which to create the context.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Description of the purpose or scope of the context.

inputs.name: project_ids
inputs.about: Project IDs to which the context applies. Pass an empty list to create a global context that applies to all projects.

inputs.name: issue_type_ids
inputs.about: Issue type IDs to which the context applies. Pass an empty list to make the context apply to all issue types.

tools.name: Create Filter
tools.description: Create a Jira saved filter with a required name and optional JQL query.

inputs.name: jql
inputs.about: Optional JQL query that defines which issues the filter returns.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Unique name for the saved filter.

inputs.name: expand
inputs.about: Comma-separated response expansions. Supported values include sharedUsers and subscriptions.

inputs.name: favourite
inputs.about: Whether to select the new filter as a favourite.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Description of the saved filter.

inputs.name: edit_permissions
inputs.about: Groups, projects, roles, or users allowed to edit the filter.

inputs.name: share_permissions
inputs.about: Groups, projects, roles, or users allowed to view the filter.

inputs.name: override_share_permissions
inputs.about: Whether to allow creation with any share permissions. This requires the Administer Jira global permission.

tools.name: Create Group
tools.description: Creates a new group in Jira with the specified name.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the group to create. Must be unique within the Jira instance.

tools.description: Creates a Jira issue in a specified project with standard and additional custom fields, including fields required by the project. If the assignee is not available on the create screen, the issue may be created without the requested assignee; the omission is reported.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.about: List of labels to categorize the issue; new labels are created if they don't exist.

inputs.name: parent
inputs.about: Parent issue key (e.g., 'PROJ-123') or issue ID. IMPORTANT: This field should ONLY be used when creating sub-task issue types (e.g., 'Sub-task', 'Subtask'). It is required for sub-tasks. Jira enforces strict hierarchy rules: standard issue types (Task, Story, Bug) can ONLY have Sub-tasks as children

inputs.name: summary

inputs.name: assignee

Must be a valid Jira account ID in one of these formats: (1) Cloud format with tenant ID and UUID: '712020:xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx', or (2) Legacy 24-character hex string: '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g'. inputs.name: due_date
inputs.about: Expected resolution date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

inputs.name: priority

inputs.about: Account ID of the user reporting the issue. Defaults to the API request user if unspecified.

inputs.name: versions
inputs.about: List of IDs for versions affected by this issue; versions must exist in the project.

inputs.name: sprint_id
inputs.about: ID of the sprint to assign this issue to. The issue will be added to the specified sprint if provided.

inputs.name: components
inputs.about: List of component IDs (e.g., '10000'); components must already exist in the project.

inputs.name: issue_type
inputs.about: REQUIRED. Type of the issue - must be valid for the target project as available types vary by project configuration. inputs.about: Detailed description of the issue. Accepts either: (1) A plain text or Markdown string (converted to ADF internally), or (2) A pre-formatted Atlassian Document Format (ADF) dict with keys 'type'='doc', 'version'=1, and 'content' array. inputs.name: environment
inputs.about: Environment details. Accepts either: (1) A plain text or Markdown string (converted to ADF internally), or (2) A pre-formatted Atlassian Document Format (ADF) dict with keys 'type'='doc', 'version'=1, and 'content' array. When passing ADF directly, formatting is preserved as-is.

inputs.name: project_key
inputs.about: REQUIRED. Key of the Jira project where the issue will be created (e.g., 'KAN', 'DEV', 'PROJ'). This is the short uppercase code that appears in issue keys like 'PROJ-123'. inputs.name: fix_versions
inputs.about: List of IDs for versions where the issue is/will be fixed; versions must exist in the project.

inputs.name: assignee_name
inputs.about: Name or email of the user to assign the issue to. Can be either an email address (e.g., 'john@company.com') or display name (e.g., 'John Doe'). The system will auto-detect the type and search accordingly. Ignored if assignee (account ID) is also provided. NOTE: Slack user IDs (e.g., 'U02QWF25EQ6') a

tools.name: Link Issues
tools.description: Links two Jira issues using a specified link type with optional comment.

inputs.name: comment
inputs.about: An optional textual comment to add to the created issue link, providing additional context.

inputs.name: link_type
inputs.about: The name of the issue link type to create (e.g., 'Blocks', 'Relates', 'Duplicate', 'Cloners'). Provide either link_type or link_type_id. Use the JIRA_GET_ISSUE_LINK_TYPES action to retrieve valid link type names for your Jira instance.

inputs.name: hierarchy_level

inputs.name: project_ids

inputs.name: include_collapsed_fields

tools.name: Delete Attachment

inputs.name: attachment_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the attachment to delete.

tools.name: Delete Comment
tools.description: Deletes a specific comment from a Jira issue using its ID and the issue's ID/key; requires user permission to delete comments on the issue.

tools.description: Permanently deletes a Jira issue by ID or key, optionally deleting its subtasks as well. Obtain explicit user confirmation before calling.

inputs.about: The ID or key of the issue to delete.

inputs.about: The case-sensitive Jira issue ID or issue key.

tools.name: Delete Issue Link

inputs.about: The unique identifier of the issue link to delete.

tools.name: Delete Statuses
tools.description: Deletes one to fifty Jira workflow statuses by identifier.

inputs.name: status_ids
inputs.about: IDs of one to fifty Jira statuses to delete.

tools.name: Delete Version
tools.description: Deletes a Jira version and optionally reassigns its issues.

inputs.name: version_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the version to be deleted.

inputs.name: move_fix_issues_to
inputs.about: The ID of an alternative version to which issues with the deleted version as their fix version will be moved. If unspecified or null, these issues will remain unassigned from a fix version.

inputs.name: move_affected_issues_to
inputs.about: The ID of an alternative version to which issues with the deleted version as their affected version will be moved. If unspecified or null, these issues will remain unassigned from an affected version.

tools.name: Delete Worklog
tools.description: Deletes a worklog from a Jira issue with estimate adjustment options.

inputs.name: worklog_id

tools.name: List Project Types
tools.description: Retrieves all Jira project types available in the instance. Use when you need to discover available project types or list all types without filtering by a specific key.

tools.name: List Screen Tab Fields
tools.description: Return the fields configured on one Jira screen tab.

inputs.name: tab_id

inputs.name: screen_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the Jira screen containing the tab.

inputs.name: project_key

tools.name: List Screen Tabs
tools.description: List the tabs configured on one Jira screen.

inputs.name: screen_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the Jira screen whose tabs to list.

inputs.name: project_key
inputs.about: Project key used to return tabs relevant to the project's screen configuration.

tools.name: List Sprints
tools.description: Retrieves paginated sprints from a Jira board with optional state filtering.

inputs.name: state
inputs.about: Filters sprints by state. Accepts single value ('active') or comma-separated values ('active,closed'). Valid states: 'future', 'active', 'closed'. Returns all states if omitted.

inputs.name: board_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the Jira board. Must be a Scrum board ID; Kanban boards do not support sprints and will return no results. Use JIRA_LIST_BOARDS to identify the correct board.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.about: 0-based starting index for pagination. Increment by `max_results` each iteration; stop when response field `isLast` is true.

inputs.name: max_results

tools.name: List Updated Worklogs
tools.description: Return one updated-worklog checkpoint page. Jira omits updates from the minute before each request, so delay the final checkpoint read by at least one minute before advancing a durable checkpoint.

inputs.name: since
inputs.about: Return worklogs updated after this Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Use the prior page's until value to continue checkpoint synchronization. Jira omits updates from the minute before each request, so delay the final checkpoint read by at least one minute.

inputs.name: expand
inputs.about: Additional worklog information to include. Jira currently accepts 'properties'.

tools.name: Move Issues to Sprint
tools.description: Moves one or more Jira issues to a specified active sprint.

inputs.name: issues
inputs.about: A list of issue keys (e.g., 'PROJ-123') to be moved to the specified sprint.

inputs.name: sprint_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier for the target sprint. Must belong to the same board/project as the issues being moved.

inputs.name: rank_after_issue
inputs.about: The issue key or ID to rank the moved issues after. If specified, the moved issues will be placed immediately after this issue in the sprint backlog.

inputs.name: rank_before_issue
inputs.about: The issue key or ID to rank the moved issues before. If specified, the moved issues will be placed immediately before this issue in the sprint backlog.

inputs.name: rank_custom_field_id
inputs.about: The ID of the rank custom field to use for ordering. This is typically the 'Rank' field ID in your Jira instance. Only needed if you have multiple rank fields.

inputs.name: group_id
inputs.about: The ID of the group to remove the user from. Either group_name or group_id must be provided.

inputs.name: account_id
inputs.about: The Atlassian account ID of the user to remove from the group. System and app accounts cannot be modified; attempting removal returns a 400 'User not modifiable' error.

inputs.name: group_name
inputs.about: The name of the group to remove the user from. Either group_name or group_id must be provided.

tools.name: Remove User from Project Role
tools.description: Removes a user or group from a project role.

inputs.name: role_id
inputs.about: The ID of the project role to remove the user from. Use get_project_roles action to find available role IDs.

inputs.name: group_name
inputs.about: The name of the group to remove from the project role. Either user_account_id or group_name must be provided.

inputs.name: user_account_id
inputs.about: The Atlassian account ID of the user to remove from the project role. Either user_account_id or group_name must be provided.

inputs.name: project_id_or_key
inputs.about: The project ID (numeric) or project key (e.g., 'PROJ') of the project.

tools.name: Remove Watcher from Issue
tools.description: Removes a user from an issue's watcher list by account ID.

inputs.name: account_id
inputs.about: The account ID of the user to remove from the issue's watchers list. Must be an account ID, not a username; retrieve via JIRA_GET_CURRENT_USER or JIRA_FIND_USERS.

inputs.name: issue_id_or_key
inputs.about: The ID or key of the issue.

inputs.name: jql
inputs.about: A JQL (Jira Query Language) expression to search for issues. tools.name: Search Dashboards
tools.description: Tool to search for Jira dashboards with filtering, sorting, and pagination support. Use when you need to find dashboards by name, owner, sharing permissions, or status. Supports filtering by owner account ID, group, project, and dashboard name.

inputs.name: owner
inputs.about: User name used to return dashboards with the matching owner.name. This parameter is deprecated due to privacy changes - use accountId instead. Cannot be used with accountId parameter.

inputs.name: expand
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of properties to expand. Options: description, owner, viewUrl, favourite, favouritedCount, sharePermissions, editPermissions, isWritable.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Enum for dashboard status filter.

inputs.name: groupId
inputs.about: Group ID used to return dashboards that are shared with a group matching sharePermissions.group.groupId. Cannot be used with groupname parameter.

inputs.name: orderBy
inputs.about: Enum for dashboard ordering options.

inputs.name: startAt
inputs.about: The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).

inputs.name: accountId
inputs.about: User account ID used to return dashboards with the matching owner.accountId. This parameter cannot be used with the owner parameter.

inputs.name: groupname
inputs.about: Group name used to return dashboards that are shared with a group matching sharePermissions.group.name. As a group's name can change, use of groupId is recommended. Cannot be used with groupId parameter.

inputs.name: projectId
inputs.about: Project ID used to return dashboards that are shared with a project matching sharePermissions.project.id.

inputs.name: maxResults
inputs.about: The maximum number of items to return per page.

inputs.name: dashboardName
inputs.about: String used to perform a case-insensitive partial match with dashboard name.

inputs.name: properties

inputs.name: reconcile_issues

inputs.name: updated_after

inputs.about: Filter issues updated before this date (YYYY-MM-DD format).

inputs.name: next_page_token

inputs.name: issue_id_or_key

inputs.name: property_key

inputs.name: issue_id_or_key
inputs.about: ID or key of the Jira issue whose property will be set.

tools.name: Update Sprint
tools.description: Partially updates a sprint without clearing omitted fields. Changing state from future to active starts the sprint and requires start_date and end_date (on the sprint or in this request); changing active to closed completes the sprint, which cannot be reopened.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: Sprint identifier to include in the request body. This is distinct from sprint_id, which selects the sprint in the URL path.

inputs.name: goal
inputs.about: New sprint goal. An empty string clears the goal; omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: New sprint name. Omit this field to preserve the current name.

inputs.name: self
inputs.about: REST API URI for the sprint. Omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: state
inputs.about: New sprint lifecycle state. future->active starts the sprint and needs start_date and end_date; active->closed completes it irreversibly. Omit this field to preserve the current state.

inputs.name: end_date
inputs.about: New sprint end date and time in ISO 8601 format. Omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: sprint_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the sprint to update. Use JIRA_LIST_SPRINTS to find sprint IDs for a board.

inputs.name: start_date
inputs.about: New sprint start date and time in ISO 8601 format. Omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: created_date
inputs.about: Sprint creation date and time. Omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: origin_board_id
inputs.about: Identifier of the board where the sprint originated. Omit this field to preserve it.

tools.name: Update Version

inputs.name: driver

inputs.name: expand
inputs.about: Comma-separated version details to include: operations, issuesstatus, driver, or approvers.

inputs.name: archived
inputs.about: Whether the version is archived. Omit this field to preserve its current state.

inputs.name: released
inputs.about: Whether the version is released. Omit this field to preserve its current state.

inputs.name: start_date
inputs.about: New work start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: version_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the Jira project version to update.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: New version description. An empty string clears the description; omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: release_date
inputs.about: New release date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit this field to preserve it.

inputs.name: move_unfixed_issues_to
inputs.about: HTTP(S) self-link URI of the destination version that receives unresolved issues when this version is released.
